what: CorVel is a managed-care company focused on workers’ compensation. It handles claims for employers and insurers, reviews and reprices medical bills, runs networks of preferred doctors and pharmacies, manages cases so injured workers return to work sooner, and offers payment integrity services to group health plans. Its fiscal year ends in March.
customers: Self-insured employers, insurance companies, third-party administrators, government agencies and group health plans in the United States.
money: Third-party claims administration and case management for workers’ compensation and auto claims.
Bill review, preferred provider networks, pharmacy and payment integrity services.
moat: CorVel’s advantage is its integrated software platform, CareMC, combined with decades of claims data and a reputation for lower claim costs. Employers that hand over their claims process rarely switch, because migrating years of open claims is painful and the savings from better medical cost control are hard to replicate. That stickiness shows in steady growth and a debt-free balance sheet.
risks: The shares trade at about 38 times earnings and 22 times EV/EBITDA, a premium that assumes growth continues.
Gross margin is only about 24%, so wage inflation for claims staff and nurses can squeeze profits.
Workers’ compensation claim volumes depend on employment levels and workplace safety trends.
Large private rivals such as Sedgwick have more scale and can win big accounts on price.
The company gives little guidance and has few analysts, so news can move the stock sharply.
opportunities: Revenue grew from $646M in fiscal 2022 to just over $1B over the last twelve months, with net income almost doubling.
The company has no debt and $270M of cash, and has steadily bought back shares.
Payment integrity for group health plans is a large new market for its bill review technology.
AI tools can raise claims productivity, which would lift margins in a labour-heavy business.
watch: New third-party administrator contracts, growth in payment integrity, gross margin trends and share buybacks.
view: CorVel is one of those small, quietly excellent companies that people discover by looking at a long-term chart. It has compounded revenue and earnings for years by handling workers’ compensation claims better and more cheaply than larger rivals, with a single in-house software platform and no debt. Net income rose from $66M in fiscal 2022 to $122M over the last twelve months, on revenue that crossed $1B.

The problem is that everybody now knows. At about 38 times earnings and 2.8% free cash flow yield, the stock prices in continued double-digit growth and margin expansion. That is possible, because claims administration contracts are long and sticky and the payment integrity business opens a much larger market, but gross margins near 24% leave little buffer if labour costs rise faster than pricing.

This is a great business at a full price. The investment turns on whether CorVel can keep winning large administrator contracts from Sedgwick and others while using technology to lift margins. I would own it happily on a pullback, but at today’s multiple I would wait: the business is likely to do well, the stock may simply track earnings growth rather than beat it.
bull: CorVel keeps taking claims administration share and payment integrity becomes a second growth engine, lifting margins.
bear: Growth slows to mid-single digits and the 38 times multiple compresses even though the business stays healthy.
